<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ba9da0839e52880750aff3efeab5e7a8b95ebe6d` — the merge of head `0e19bd82a1223382bc0a1292e8f235ac0de03715` into base `c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ba9da0839e52880750aff3efeab5e7a8b95ebe6d && git checkout ba9da0839e52880750aff3efeab5e7a8b95ebe6d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7 0e19bd82a1223382bc0a1292e8f235ac0de03715 && git checkout -B drift-repro c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7 && git merge --no-ff 0e19bd82a1223382bc0a1292e8f235ac0de03715

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs c110853e59ef75b9a137178aefd1a9bd495fe2e7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b54563589bed39b3b009e5c4d785260d94f8294e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/inbox-message.object.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/notification-delivery.object.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/notification-receipt.object.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/admin-copy-vocabulary.test.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/objects/inbox-message-mine-view.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/notifications.hono.integration.test.ts + read in the cited code, not reviewed: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts (`managedBy`, `resolveCrudAffordances`), packages/spec/src/data/api-derivation.ts (`apiExposureDenialReason`), packages/spec/src/data/managed-api-affordance.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`reconcileManagedApiMethods`), packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts (`apiAccessDenialFromEnable`, `enforceApiAccess`) with crud-routes.ts, batch-routes.ts and data-action-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/system-write-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-planning.ts (`outlivesOrganization`), packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts, packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts, messaging-service.ts, fan-out-system-context.ts, inbox-system-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/notifications.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useInboxBell.ts, sharedUserFeeds.ts, useHomeInbox.ts, docs/adr/0030-notification-platform-convergence.md

Check-runs on this head (the PR is a draft): every run that started concluded `success`. That covers Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and its roll-up, Build Core, all four Type Check families and the TypeScript roll-up, all eight Lint families and their roll-up, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, the docs-drift flag and the Dogfood Regression Gate job.

Did not run (skipped): the Dogfood Regression Gate shards (n/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Lint UI, the Test UI shards (n/16), UI Published Artifacts, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, and the two opt-in harnesses. The Dogfood job's green therefore carries no shard result. The full dogfood battery the seat's ruling owes on the final head has no CI verdict; the only evidence is the dev's local run, which is not a gate verdict here.

### ① Derived judgments

- **REST writes now 405: right.** `enable.apiMethods: ['get','list']` makes `apiExposureDenialReason` answer `method-not-allowed` for create, update and delete. `enforceApiAccess` sends `405 OBJECT_API_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` before any handler, for every persona. Bulk, import, upsert, restore and purge are refused by the same whitelist. `get`, `list` and the verbs derived from `list` (search, export, aggregate) are unchanged. The wire test pins POST, PATCH and DELETE (Test Core green).
- **Console affordances: right.** The `engine-owned` bucket resolves create, import, edit and delete to `false`. No `userActions` block is needed.
- **Mark-read and mark-all-read: right, untouched.** Neither path writes `sys_inbox_message`. Both write `sys_notification_receipt` under `INBOX_SYSTEM_CONTEXT`, keyed on the session's user id. The console calls `POST /notifications/read` and `/read/all` (`useInboxBell.ts`), not the data door. The wire test's control pins `readCount: 1` and unread 1 to 0.
- **First-party writers: none refused.** The inbox channel inserts under `FAN_OUT_SYSTEM_CONTEXT`. The 90-day reaper deletes under its own `isSystem` context. The security guard passes `isSystem` and context-less writes. No `ui/` code, seed or example writes the object; the console only reads it.
- **User-context engine write refused 403: right, but not pinned in this diff.** It is the generic plugin-security guard keyed on `managedBy`, with its own tests.
- **Organization delete moves: right against the published rule.** `outlivesOrganization` reads the bucket, so inbox rows are no longer counted and are kept. The changeset declares it.
- **Field-help and FK-note rewrites: right.** The three rewrites on delivery and receipt, and the three on inbox, state what the code does. `delivery_id` is written `null` by both receipt writers and omitted by the inbox insert. The `Actor` to `Triggered By` relabel is a label-only change.
- **Vocabulary guard: right.** The two new patterns catch the old strings in English and Chinese, and the population now asserts `sys_inbox_message`.

### ② Semver level

Patch + BREAKING + ADR-0087 `not-required` + `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` + `Metadata-protocol: none` matches AGENTS.md step 3. No authorable key, value or type moves, so it is a non-protocol narrowing at `patch`. Only `@objectstack/service-messaging` publishes a change; the runtime file is a test. `Check Changeset` is green.

One gap in what the changeset tells an upgrader: see ④ S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`:** empty. Nothing to answer.
- **"delivery_id is inert on inbox and receipt rows":** confirmed in the tree. A declared link that no writer fills is an implement-or-retire gap. The PR does not narrow it; it only words the help honestly. Escalated: the seat owes the card it said it would file at ACCEPT. It is not filed yet.
- **"Removing apiMethods alone stays green":** answered, and the report's wording is wrong. What was measured is the whitelist widened to all five verbs, which `reconcileManagedApiMethods` strips. An absent whitelist is out of that function's scope (`checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` returns nothing for a missing array), so REST would admit the write. In this test harness, which mounts no security plugin, a true removal would answer 201 and turn both the wire pin and the declaration pin red. The whitelist is therefore load-bearing and pinned, not redundant. The tree is correct; only the PR body and the report misstate it.
- **Engine-owned rows outlive organization delete (family question):** escalated. The report says "noted, not filed", so the seat's card is still owed.
- **Deviations:** the widened runtime test file is covered by ruling 6809703302. The sibling help-text fix is forced by the widened guard and stays inside the claimed surface. Accepted.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away.**

- ADR-0030 on `main` says no producer writes an inbox row directly. The spec's `engine-owned` bucket is defined as "no user writes, ever" and names the messaging pipeline. The default permission sets already call the inbox channel the object's writer and give members read only. The four sibling objects carry the same pair.
- The open generic door was an undeclared bypass, and it could not deliver what it appeared to offer: a row written through it has no `notification_id`, so it can never be marked read.
- Attempts to break it failed. A recipient can still mark read. No engine-side writer is refused. Reads are unchanged.
- Organization delete no longer cleans or counts these rows; they age out at 90 days under the system reaper. That is the published `outlivesOrganization` rule, and the owed family card carries the rest.

Findings:

- **S1, should-fix: the upgrade strands rows already written through the old door.** On `main` an administrator could DELETE a hand-written row (200). After this PR the same DELETE answers 405 and no user-context door remains. Those rows have no `notification_id`, so they stay on the recipient's unread badge until their 90-day expiry. The changeset says existing rows are "kept and served as before" and gives no remedy. Fix with either one sentence in the changeset (delete inbox rows that have no notification id over the data API before upgrading, else they stay unread until expiry) or a system-context sweep of such rows. The changeset sentence is the smaller fix.
- **N1, nit: the changeset omits a consequence of the moved answer.** After an organization delete, the kept rows are still served in the recipient's bell for up to 90 days, because `listInbox` keys on `user_id` alone. Add this to the family card as a datum.
- **N2, nit: the new help text paraphrases an inert-column notice.** "Not filled in for in-app messages" and "Not currently filled in" are the kind of notice the same guard bans as `Inert today`. It is accurate and plain; the cure is the `delivery_id` card, not wording.
- **N3, nit: the rollout-phase pattern may over-match.** `\bP\d+\b` would also refuse future legitimate copy such as "P95" or "P1 priority". Nothing in the tree trips it today.
- **N4, nit: correct the PR body and report sentence on the partial ablation**, per ③.

S1 earns a delta review of its fix. No must-fix.
